prompt: What's a problem that your generation solved that younger people don't appreciate?

I mean, when I was in school, we didn't have all these student loans and financial aid like you do now. We had to work part-time jobs, and we had to be careful with our money. But we made it work.

And you know what? We came out the other side with a sense of accomplishment and a sense of responsibility that I don't think a lot of younger people have today. I mean, don't get me wrong, I'm not saying it was easy. But we had to be resourceful, and we had to be smart about how we spent our money.

Now, I'm not saying that the system is perfect, and I think there are definitely ways to make it better. But I think we solved the problem of paying for college in a way that taught us valuable life skills. And I think that's something that's been lost on a lot of younger people today.

I mean, I see kids graduating from college with tens of thousands of dollars in debt, and it's just... it's not right. We didn't have that. We had to work hard, and we had to be smart about it. And I think that's something that's been lost on a lot of younger people today. (adjusts glasses)
